seed_frames.label: Quality beliefs and false sense of safety
seed_frames.argument: Water from the family mine or well does not need testing because it looks clear, flows continuously and has been consumed for generations without any perceived illness.

seed_frames.label: Tariff resistance and rejection of centralised management
seed_frames.argument: AdAM bills and charges are seen as disproportionate compared with historical local costs, leading residents to keep or reactivate their own wells to avoid mandatory charges.

seed_frames.label: Institutional distrust and perceived environmental hypocrisy
seed_frames.argument: Municipal alerts advising against drinking from public fountains are met with scepticism; residents accuse public bodies of ignoring industrial or wastewater-plant discharges into rivers.

seed_frames.label: Invisible risks and public-network supply failures
seed_frames.argument: The municipal public supply is not seen as an absolute guarantee of safety, which motivates the search for underground alternatives even without control of nitrates or bacteria.

researcher_instructions: Extract the exact argument used by residents (why they trust or reject each source), not just the general topic. Prefer short, concrete threads. Keep the corpus language in literal excerpts.
